approachQuestion.prompt:
Crossing Word Slots

A character grid contains # blocks, . empty cells, and fixed lowercase letters. An explicit ordered list of slots is supplied; each slot is a sequence of distinct nonblocked cells. Fill each slot with a distinct dictionary word of exactly its length, matching all letters already on those cells. Different slots may cross, but no cell belongs to more than two slots. Return every distinct filled grid satisfying all slots, once. Every nonblocked cell belongs to a slot.

Examples:
grid=["..",".#"], slots=[[(0,0),(0,1)],[(0,0),(1,0)]], words=["ab","ac"] -> grids ["ab","c#"] and ["ac","b#"].
grid=["z."], slots=[[(0,0),(0,1)]], words=["ab"] -> [].

Constraints: 1 <= h,w <= 6; 1 <= slots.length <= 8; 1 <= words.length <= 12. Words are distinct nonempty lowercase strings, length <= 6. No two slots have the identical ordered cell sequence. A cell can occur at most once in a slot. The input cannot be modified.

options.text: For a compatible unused word, record which slot cells were dots, write them, and clear only that recorded subset on return. Leave matching crossing letters untouched and undo word usage.
options.feedback: A letter introduced by an ancestor may be shared by a crossing slot. Clearing only this placement’s writes restores precisely the state that existed on entry.

options.text: After trying a word, clear every cell in its slot to a dot.
options.feedback: In the first example, after the second slot is undone this clears the crossing letter belonging to the first slot, corrupting the ancestor’s placement.

options.text: Reuse dictionary words freely when their letters fit.
options.feedback: For grid=["..#.."], two horizontal length-2 slots, words=["ab"], reusing "ab" would falsely report a filled grid despite the distinct-word requirement.

options.text: Copy the entire working grid and used-word flags for each compatible candidate, and recurse with those copies.
options.feedback: This is correct, but copying the entire board per child is removable: a change list records exactly the cells that need restoration.

feedback.reason: A letter introduced by an ancestor may be shared by a crossing slot. Clearing only this placement’s writes restores precisely the state that existed on entry.
details: Copy the grid and keep used-word flags. Fill slots in supplied order. Try each unused word of matching length; check all slot cells for conflicts before changing anything. Write letters only into dots, recording those cells, mark the word used, recurse, then clear only the recorded cells and unmark that word. Copy the grid after all slots are filled.

Check every crossing for consistency before writing any cell. Record only dots changed by this word and clear only those on undo; clearing shared preexisting letters would corrupt earlier slot assignments.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-15-search` only. Let N=h*w, W=words.length, S=slots.length, I be nonterminal calls and R be total grid cells copied to returned grids. Each call scans all W words; each candidate checks/writes at most six cells. Initialize a copied N-cell grid and W flags. Every cell belongs to a slot, so different full word assignments yield different filled grids. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(N + W + W·I + R) time, O(N + W + S) auxiliary space
O(N + W + I + R) time, O(N + W + S) auxiliary space
O(N + W + W·I + R) time, O(N·S + W) auxiliary space
O(N + W + R) time, O(N + W + S) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Bounded word lengths give fixed work per word trial; include grid copies.
details: The bounded word length makes each word trial constant work. All W trials are scanned at every nonterminal call; copies at terminal calls add R. Initial grid and flags add N+W.
Working grid and used flags use N+W. Each of at most S frames records at most six changed cells and the current candidate, adding S.

Let N=h*w, W=words.length, S=slots.length, I be nonterminal calls and R be total grid cells copied to returned grids. Each call scans all W words; each candidate checks/writes at most six cells. Initialize a copied N-cell grid and W flags. Every cell belongs to a slot, so different full word assignments yield different filled grids.
“O(N + W + I + R) time, O(N + W + S) auxiliary space”: All W dictionary words are scanned at each nonterminal call.
“O(N + W + W·I + R) time, O(N·S + W) auxiliary space”: The revealed method uses change lists, not a full board copy per frame.
“O(N + W + R) time, O(N + W + S) auxiliary space”: Assignments can branch, causing repeated candidate-word scans.
